greek: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἡ ζωὴ Σαρρας ἔτη ἑκατὸν εἴκοσι ἑπτά.
hint: Sarah's life comes to a hundred and twenty-seven years.

notes.text: ζωή, the chain of GEN 2:9, with the article. The Hebrew repeats *šĕnê ḥayyê śārâ*, *the years of the life of Sarah*, at the end; the Greek does not.
The numbers, plain.

reading: [[came into being|came to be, arose, was brought into existence]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[the life|the life, the means of life and substance, the existence, the way of life]] [[name:Σαρρας]] years hundred twenty seven.

greek: καὶ ἀπέθανεν Σαρρα ἐν πόλει Αρβοκ, ἥ ἐστιν ἐν τῷ κοιλώματι (αὕτη ἐστὶν Χεβρων) ἐν γῇ Χανααν. ἦλθεν δὲ Αβρααμ κόψασθαι Σαρραν καὶ πενθῆσαι.
hint: Sarah dies in the city of Arba, in the valley — that is Hebron — in Canaan; Abraham comes to mourn for her.

notes.lemma: ἐν πόλει Αρβοκ, ἥ ἐστιν ἐν τῷ κοιλώματι
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *bĕqiryat ʾarbaʿ*, *in Kiriath-arba*, with nothing after it but *that is Hebron*. The Greek has *in city Arbok, which is in the hollow*.
Rahlfs prints the parentheses; the reading keeps them.
The middle of κόπτω, *to beat one's breast* in grief; the active's *to strike, smite* is left out.
One sense, *a hollow, cavity*.

reading: and [[died off|died off, died, was put to death, was slain]] [[name:Σαρρα]] [[in city|within, inside of, and by means of city, citadel, country, body of citizens, state]] [[name:Αρβοκ]], which is [[in the hollow|within, inside of, and by means of the hollow, the cavity]] (this is [[name:Χεβρων]]) [[in earth|within, inside of, and by means of earth, land, the ground]] [[name:Χανααν]]. [[came|came, went, went back and returned, was going to and intended, came within a little of and was near]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[to beat one's breast|to beat one's breast, to mourn for]] [[name:Σαρραν]] and [[to bewail|to bewail, to lament, to mourn for]].

names.gloss: (Αρβοκ, for Hebrew Qiryat ʾarbaʿ, "city of Arba" or "city of four")
(Χεβρων, from Hebrew Ḥebrôn, usually connected with ḥeber, "company, alliance")
(Χανααν, from Hebrew Kĕnaʿan, of uncertain meaning)
(Αβρααμ, from Hebrew ʾAbrāhām, which the Hebrew of 17:5 hears in ʾab hămôn gôyim, "father of a multitude of nations")

greek: καὶ ἀνέστη Αβρααμ ἀπὸ τοῦ νεκροῦ αὐτοῦ καὶ εἶπεν τοῖς υἱοῖς Χετ λέγων
hint: Abraham rises from his dead and speaks to the sons of Heth.

notes.text: νεκρός, first *a dead body, corpse*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone adds Αβρααμ.
Rahlfs prints no punctuation at the end of the verse.

reading: and [[stood up|stood up, rose, rose to fight against, rose to go and set out]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of the dead body|of the dead body, of the corpse, of the dead]] of him and [[said|said, spoke, declared, called by name, told]] to the sons [[name:Χετ]] [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling]]

names.gloss: (Χετ, from Hebrew Ḥēt, of uncertain meaning)

greek: Πάροικος καὶ παρεπίδημος ἐγώ εἰμι μεθʼ ὑμῶν· δότε οὖν μοι κτῆσιν τάφου μεθʼ ὑμῶν, καὶ θάψω τὸν νεκρόν μου ἀπʼ ἐμοῦ.
hint: I am a sojourner and stranger among you; give me a burial plot among you, and I will bury my dead.

notes.text: No Middle Liddell entry; LSJ, one translation, *sojourning in a strange place*: plain text. 1 Peter 2:11 has ὡς παροίκους καὶ παρεπιδήμους, the pair of this verse, and Hebrews 11:13 ξένοι καὶ παρεπίδημοι of the patriarchs.
πάροικος, the chain of GEN 15:13.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *millĕpānāy*, *from before me*. The Greek has *from me*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads ἐκεῖ.
Rahlfs opens the speech, and the verse, with a capital.

reading: [[dwelling beside|dwelling beside, a neighbour, a sojourner and alien]] and sojourning in a strange place I am [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of]] you; [[give|give, grant, provide, give over and deliver up]] [[really|really, at all events, surely, so, then and therefore]] to me [[acquisition|acquisition, possession, possessions and property]] [[of a burial|of a burial and funeral, of the act of burying, of the grave and tomb]] [[in the midst of|in the midst of, among, in common, along with, with, by means of]] you, and [[I will pay the last dues to a corpse|I will pay the last dues to a corpse, I will honour with funeral rites, I will bury, I will inter]] [[the dead body|the dead body, the corpse, the dead]] of me [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] me.

greek: ἀπεκρίθησαν δὲ οἱ υἱοὶ Χετ πρὸς Αβρααμ λέγοντες
hint: The sons of Heth answer Abraham:

notes.text: ἀποκρίνομαι, the chain of GEN 18:9, in the aorist.

reading: [[gave answer to|gave answer to, replied, answered, answered charges and defended themselves]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], the sons [[name:Χετ]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling]]

greek: Μή, κύριε· ἄκουσον δὲ ἡμῶν. βασιλεὺς παρὰ θεοῦ εἶ σὺ ἐν ἡμῖν· ἐν τοῖς ἐκλεκτοῖς μνημείοις ἡμῶν θάψον τὸν νεκρόν σου· οὐδεὶς γὰρ ἡμῶν τὸ μνημεῖον αὐτοῦ κωλύσει ἀπὸ σοῦ τοῦ θάψαι τὸν νεκρόν σου ἐκεῖ.
hint: No, lord, hear us: you are a king from God among us; bury your dead in our choicest tombs.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *nĕśîʾ ʾĕlōhîm*, *a prince of God*. The Greek has *a king from God*.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *šĕmāʿēnû ʾădōnî*, *hear us, my lord*. The Greek opens with *No, lord*.
Middle Liddell's first sense carries its English only inside the Latin, *monimentum, any memorial*; LSJ, *memorial, remembrance, record*, then *tomb, monument*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus has the two words the other way round.
Rahlfs opens the speech, and the verse, with a capital.

reading: not, [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over]]; [[hear|hear, have hearing of, hear tell of, hearken and give ear, listen to and obey]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], of us. [[a king|a king, a chief, an hereditary king, a lord and master and householder, the second of the nine archons, the king of Persia]] [[from the side of|from the side of, from beside, from, near]] [[of God|God's own, divine in character]] are you in us; [[in the picked out|within, inside of, and by means of the picked out, the select]] [[memorials|memorials, remembrances, records, tombs and monuments]] of us [[pay the last dues to a corpse|pay the last dues to a corpse, honour with funeral rites, bury, inter]] [[the dead body|the dead body, the corpse, the dead]] of you; [[and not one|and not one, no one, none, naught and good for naught]] for of us [[the memorial|the memorial, the remembrance, the record, the tomb and monument]] of him [[will let|will let, will hinder, will check, will prevent, will impede]] [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] you [[to pay the last dues to a corpse|to pay the last dues to a corpse, to honour with funeral rites, to bury, to inter]] [[the dead body|the dead body, the corpse, the dead]] of you [[there|there, in that place]].

greek: ἀναστὰς δὲ Αβρααμ προσεκύνησεν τῷ λαῷ τῆς γῆς, τοῖς υἱοῖς Χετ,
hint: Abraham rises and bows to the people of the land, the sons of Heth,

notes.text: προσκυνέω, the chain of GEN 18:2, with the dative.

reading: [[having stood up|having stood up, having risen, having risen to fight against, having risen to go and set out]] [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[made obeisance|made obeisance, fell down and worshipped, worshipped, adored, did reverence to, made the salam, prostrated himself before]] [[to the people|to the people, to the men, to the soldiers, to the land-army, to the common men, to the folk, to the Jews, to the Christians]] [[of the earth|of the land, of the dry ground, of the terrestrial realm]], to the sons [[name:Χετ]],

greek: καὶ ἐλάλησεν πρὸς αὐτοὺς Αβρααμ λέγων Εἰ ἔχετε τῇ ψυχῇ ὑμῶν ὥστε θάψαι τὸν νεκρόν μου ἀπὸ προσώπου μου, ἀκούσατέ μου καὶ λαλήσατε περὶ ἐμοῦ Εφρων τῷ τοῦ Σααρ,
hint: If you are willing that I bury my dead, hear me and speak for me to Ephron son of Zohar,

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾim-yēš ʾet-napšĕkem*, *if it is your will*. The Greek has *if you have it in your breath*.
The article with the genitive, *the one of Saar*, Ephron's father; `to the of`, as the articles stand.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

reading: and [[talked|talked, chatted, prattled, babbled, said, talked of, spoke, chattered, chirped]] [[toward|toward, facing, oriented to, in living motion and address toward]] them [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[saying|saying, speaking, declaring, calling by name, telling]] if [[you have|you have, you hold, you possess, you keep, you hold fast, you bear up against and support]] [[to the breath|to the breath, to the life, to the spirit, to life and death, to the ghost, to the departed soul]] of you [[so as to|so as to, as to, on the condition that, and so and therefore and consequently, as and as being, since it was]] [[to pay the last dues to a corpse|to pay the last dues to a corpse, to honour with funeral rites, to bury, to inter]] [[the dead body|the dead body, the corpse, the dead]] of me [[from|from, away from, far from, apart from]] [[of face|of face, of visage, of countenance, of look, of outward appearance]] of me, [[hear|hear, have hearing of, hear tell of, hearken and give ear, listen to and obey]] of me and [[talk|talk, chat, prattle, babble, say, talk of, speak, chatter, chirp]] [[round about|round about, around, about and near, about and for and on account of, about and concerning, for very]] me to [[name:Εφρων]] to the of [[name:Σααρ]],

names.gloss: (Εφρων, from Hebrew ʿEprôn, of uncertain meaning)
(Σααρ, from Hebrew Ṣōḥar, of uncertain meaning)

greek: καὶ δότω μοι τὸ σπήλαιον τὸ διπλοῦν, ὅ ἐστιν αὐτῷ, τὸ ὂν ἐν μέρει τοῦ ἀγροῦ αὐτοῦ· ἀργυρίου τοῦ ἀξίου δότω μοι αὐτὸ ἐν ὑμῖν εἰς κτῆσιν μνημείου.
hint: that he give me the double cave in his field, for its full price, as a burial holding among you.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *mĕʿārat hammakpēlâ*, *the cave of Machpelah*. The Greek has *the double cave*.
Filed under διπλόος, *twofold, double*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads μερίδι, and δότε for the second δότω.

reading: and [[let give|let give, let grant, let provide, let give over and deliver up]] to me [[the grotto|the grotto, the cave, the cavern]] the [[twofold|twofold, double, double-minded and treacherous]], which is to him, the being [[in part|within, inside of, and by means of part, share, one's portion and heritage and lot, one's turn, the part one takes in and the part assigned, division]] [[of the field|of the field, of the lands, of the farm, of the country]] of him; [[of a piece of silver|of a piece of silver, of a silver coin, of money and a sum of money and cash, of silver]] the [[weighing as much|weighing as much, of like value, worth as much as, worthy and goodly, of a proper value and cheap, deserved and meet and due, sufficient for, worthy of and deserving and meet for]] [[let give|let give, let grant, let provide, let give over and deliver up]] to me it in you [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[acquisition|acquisition, possession, possessions and property]] [[of memorial|of memorial, of remembrance, of record, of tomb and monument]].

greek: Εφρων δὲ ἐκάθητο ἐν μέσῳ τῶν υἱῶν Χετ· ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ Εφρων ὁ Χετταῖος πρὸς Αβρααμ εἶπεν ἀκουόντων τῶν υἱῶν Χετ καὶ πάντων τῶν εἰσπορευομένων εἰς τὴν πόλιν λέγων
hint: Ephron sits among the sons of Heth; Ephron the Hittite answers Abraham in the hearing of all who enter the city:

notes.text: The genitive absolute, `of hearing`, as καθημένου at 18:1.
μέσος, the chain of GEN 2:9, after ἐν.
The article before the people's name is not printed.

names.gloss: (Χετταῖος, the man of Χετ, Heth; Hebrew Ḥittî)

greek: Παρʼ ἐμοὶ γενοῦ, κύριε, καὶ ἄκουσόν μου. τὸν ἀγρὸν καὶ τὸ σπήλαιον τὸ ἐν αὐτῷ σοι δίδωμι· ἐναντίον πάντων τῶν πολιτῶν μου δέδωκά σοι· θάψον τὸν νεκρόν σου.
hint: Stay with me, lord, and hear me: the field and the cave in it I give you before all my countrymen; bury your dead.

notes.lemma: Παρʼ ἐμοὶ γενοῦ, κύριε, καὶ ἄκουσόν μου
notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *lōʾ-ʾădōnî šĕmāʿēnî*, *no, my lord, hear me*. The Greek has *be beside me, lord, and hear me*.
πολίτης is first *a member of a city* or *state*. The Hebrew is *bĕnê-ʿammî*, *the sons of my people*.
[[flag]] The Berlin papyrus, 911, has it; Codex Alexandrinus leaves it out.
Rahlfs opens the speech, and the verse, with a capital.

reading: [[beside|beside, alongside of, by, at, before, with]] me [[come into being|come to be, arise, be brought into existence]], [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over]], and [[hear|hear, have hearing of, hear tell of, hearken and give ear, listen to and obey]] of me. [[the field|the field, the lands, the farm, the country]] and [[the grotto|the grotto, the cave, the cavern]] the in it to you [[I give|I give, I am ready to give and offer, I grant, I provide, I give over and deliver up]]; [[in the presence of|in the presence of, before, opposite and face to face, against]] [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single]] [[of the members of a city|of the members of a city and state, of the citizens and freemen]] of me [[I have given|I have given and it stands given, I have granted and it stands granted, I have provided and it stands provided, I have given over and delivered up and it stands so]] to you; [[pay the last dues to a corpse|pay the last dues to a corpse, honour with funeral rites, bury, inter]] [[the dead body|the dead body, the corpse, the dead]] of you.

notes.text: Rahlfs prints no punctuation at the end of the verse.

greek: καὶ εἶπεν τῷ Εφρων εἰς τὰ ὦτα τοῦ λαοῦ τῆς γῆς Ἐπειδὴ πρὸς ἐμοῦ εἶ, ἄκουσόν μου· τὸ ἀργύριον τοῦ ἀγροῦ λαβὲ παρʼ ἐμοῦ, καὶ θάψω τὸν νεκρόν μου ἐκεῖ.
hint: and says to Ephron: since you are on my side, hear me — take the price of the field from me, and I will bury my dead there.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾak ʾim-ʾattâ lû šĕmāʿēnî*, *but if you will, hear me*. The Greek has *since you are on my side*.
πρός with the genitive, first *from, from forth*, then *on the side of*.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus puts ἐναντίον παντός before it.
Capitalised because it opens direct speech, as Rahlfs prints it; listed in `speech` so the checks do not take it for a proper name.

notes.text: Rahlfs prints no punctuation at the end of the verse.

greek: Οὐχί, κύριε· ἀκήκοα. γῆ τετρακοσίων διδράχμων ἀργυρίου, ἀνὰ μέσον ἐμοῦ καὶ σοῦ τί ἂν εἴη τοῦτο; σὺ δὲ τὸν νεκρόν σου θάψον.
hint: No, lord, I have heard: land worth four hundred didrachms of silver — what is that between you and me? Bury your dead.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾădōnî šĕmāʿēnî*, *my lord, hear me*. The Greek has *no, lord; I have heard*.
[[flag]] The Hebrew is *ʾarbaʿ mēʾōt šeqel-kesep*, *four hundred shekels of silver*. The Greek has the didrachm.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus reads γάρ; a few witnesses have γῆ.
Rahlfs opens the speech, and the verse, with a capital.

reading: not, [[lord|lord, master, the one having power and authority over]]; [[I have heard|I have heard and it stands so, I have had hearing of and it stands so, I have heard tell of and it stands so, I have hearkened and given ear and it stands so, I have listened to and obeyed and it stands so]]. [[earth|earth, land, the ground]] four hundred [[of coins of two drachms|of coins of two drachms, of half-shekels]] [[of a piece of silver|of a piece of silver, of a silver coin, of money and a sum of money and cash, of silver]], [[up to middle|up to, up along, and throughout the middle, in the middle, the centre, mid, between two]] of me and of you what ever may be [[this|this, the nearer, what follows]]? you [[but|but, however, whereas, on the other hand]], [[the dead body|the dead body, the corpse, the dead]] of you [[pay the last dues to a corpse|pay the last dues to a corpse, honour with funeral rites, bury, inter]].

greek: καὶ ἤκουσεν Αβρααμ τοῦ Εφρων, καὶ ἀπεκατέστησεν Αβρααμ τῷ Εφρων τὸ ἀργύριον, ὃ ἐλάλησεν εἰς τὰ ὦτα τῶν υἱῶν Χετ, τετρακόσια δίδραχμα ἀργυρίου δοκίμου ἐμπόροις.
hint: Abraham listens to Ephron and weighs out to him the silver he named, four hundred didrachms of approved silver, current with merchants.

notes.text: [[flag]] The Hebrew is *wayyišqōl*, *and he weighed out*. The Greek has ἀποκαθίστημι, *to re-establish, restore*.
δόκιμος is first *assayed, examined, tested*, of metals; ἔμπορος first *one who goes on shipboard as a passenger*, *a merchant, trader* its third.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone reads τῷ.

greek: καὶ ἔστη ὁ ἀγρὸς Εφρων, ὃς ἦν ἐν τῷ διπλῷ σπηλαίῳ, ὅς ἐστιν κατὰ πρόσωπον Μαμβρη, ὁ ἀγρὸς καὶ τὸ σπήλαιον, ὃ ἦν ἐν αὐτῷ, καὶ πᾶν δένδρον, ὃ ἦν ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ, ὅ ἐστιν ἐν τοῖς ὁρίοις αὐτοῦ κύκλῳ,

notes.text: The second aorist of ἵστημι, intransitive, as at 18:2; the Hebrew *wayyāqom*, *and it stood*, of the transfer.

[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone leaves out ἐν.

hint: became Abraham's possession before the sons of Heth and all who entered the city.

notes.text: κτῆσις is first *acquisition*, then *possession*.

reading: to [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[acquisition|acquisition, possession, possessions and property]] [[in the presence of|in the presence of, before, opposite and face to face, against]] of the sons [[name:Χετ]] and [[of all|of all, of the whole, of every, of every single]] [[of the ones going into|of the ones going into, of the ones entering]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[the city|the city, the citadel, the country, the body of citizens, the state]].

greek: μετὰ ταῦτα ἔθαψεν Αβρααμ Σαρραν τὴν γυναῖκα αὐτοῦ ἐν τῷ σπηλαίῳ τοῦ ἀγροῦ τῷ διπλῷ, ὅ ἐστιν ἀπέναντι Μαμβρη (αὕτη ἐστὶν Χεβρων) ἐν τῇ γῇ Χανααν.
hint: Then Abraham buries Sarah in the double cave of the field facing Mamre — that is Hebron — in Canaan.

notes.text: The repeated article before the adjective, plain `the`.
ἀπέναντι, the chain of GEN 3:24.

reading: [[into the middle of|into the middle of, coming among, in pursuit and quest of, after]] [[these|these, the nearer, what follows]] [[paid the last dues to a corpse|paid the last dues to a corpse, honoured with funeral rites, buried, interred]] [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[name:Σαρραν]] [[the woman|the woman, the mistress and lady, the wife and spouse]] of him [[in the grotto|within, inside of, and by means of the grotto, the cave, the cavern]] [[of the field|of the field, of the lands, of the farm, of the country]] the [[twofold|twofold, double, double-minded and treacherous]], which is [[opposite|opposite, against]] [[name:Μαμβρη]] (this is [[name:Χεβρων]]) [[in the earth|within, inside of, and by means of the land, the dry ground, the terrestrial realm]] [[name:Χανααν]].

greek: καὶ ἐκυρώθη ὁ ἀγρὸς καὶ τὸ σπήλαιον, ὃ ἦν ἐν αὐτῷ, τῷ Αβρααμ εἰς κτῆσιν τάφου παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Χετ.
hint: The field and its cave are made over to Abraham as a burial holding by the sons of Heth.

notes.text: κυρόω is first *to make valid, confirm, ratify*; the passive, `was made valid`.
[[flag]] Codex Alexandrinus alone leaves out ἐν; Codex Sinaiticus has it.

reading: and [[was made valid|was made valid, was confirmed, was ratified, was determined, was decided]] [[the field|the field, the lands, the farm, the country]] and [[the grotto|the grotto, the cave, the cavern]], which was, and kept on being as a standing and continuing condition and not a momentary one, in it, to [[name:Αβρααμ]] [[into|into, to, in, rest in]] [[acquisition|acquisition, possession, possessions and property]] [[of a burial|of a burial and funeral, of the act of burying, of the grave and tomb]] [[from the side of|from the side of, from beside, from, near]] of the sons [[name:Χετ]].
